captions.detailed: A refractor spotting scope mounted on an alt-azimuth tripod. The assembly features a dark cylindrical main optical tube with a rear eyepiece, mounted on a dual-jointed ball-head bracket. The tripod base consists of three spread legs with flat rectangular feet, joined to a central vertical column. The spotting scope can rotate continuously on its horizontal pan bearing and tilt vertically via a revolute joint.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a refractor spotting scope on an alt-azimuth tripod. The tripod should have three angled legs with rectangular feet, supporting a central column. Mount a ball-head bracket on top of the column to allow continuous horizontal rotation, and connect a cylindrical optical tube with an eyepiece that can tilt vertically using a revolute joint.
captions.factory: Construct the tripod base using cylindrical segments for the legs and central column, combined with rectangular boxes for the feet. Create the panning head using stacked cylinders and a spherical ball joint. Build the spotting scope body using a series of concentric cylinders of varying diameters to form the main tube, objective bell, and eyepiece. Define a continuous joint for the horizontal pan bearing, and a revolute joint for the vertical pitch/tilt axis.
